Hi —

Thanks for the heads up and for attaching the usage file. We can support both approaches you mentioned; below is the recommended protocol we use for multi-entity customers to minimize reconciliation friction:

1) Preferred (single master invoice with line-level entity tags):
   - We will issue one invoice PDF labelled as the "Master Invoice" with per-line metadata: entity_code, cost_center, PO.
   - Each line will include a field "billing_entity": either GFH-INC or GFH-CLINICS and a tax flag ("vat_reverse_charge": true/false).
   - Your AR system can apply payments using the line-level references; the remittance advice will summarize totals per entity.

2) Alternative (separate invoices):
   - We can produce two legally separate invoice numbers (one per entity). This is cleaner for ledgers but increases document count.

VAT handling: for lines delivered to GFH-CLINICS where VAT reverse-charge applies, we will set tax_amount = 0 and include a note: "Reverse-charge applies per client VAT ID: [EU-VAT-12345]." Please confirm the EU VAT ID for filing.

Required fields from your side to proceed (please reply inline):
- Confirm preferred approach (master invoice with tags OR separate invoices)
- Confirm the exact VAT ID to display for Greenfield Clinics LLC
- Confirm which payment rail you will use (ACH / Wire) and whether you require multiple beneficiary accounts for entity separation

What I'll do next: attach sample mapping for June lines (invoice_map.csv) and a short remit instructions PDF for our multi-entity flows (remit_instructions.pdf). Once you confirm the above, we'll produce the invoice(s) and provide a DocuSign remit form if you need separate beneficiary confirmation.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Billing Operations
Redwood Inference
attachments: invoice_map.csv, remit_instructions.pdf
